operative_context: Concrete Mixers require a 12-hour (720 min) maintenance window as an emergency override to the standard 2-hour (120 min) rule
Maintenance windows must block rental activity and mark items as unavailable during maintenance periods
Availability status must be updated immediately when maintenance periods are created or modified
Maintenance period management allows authorized users to define, modify, and remove maintenance periods
Maintenance periods take precedence over normal availability windows
exceptions: Concrete Mixers category has a hardcoded 12-hour (720 min) maintenance window, overriding the standard 2-hour (120 min) rule until the official Maintenance Matrix is published in the next SRS version
conflicts_or_obsolete: The dynamic Maintenance Matrix referenced in SRS v1.2 is superseded by the emergency hardcoded Concrete Mixer rule effective 2026-02-20
gaps_or_uncertainties: Exact behavior depends on a category- or matrix-based rule that is not fully specified in the retrieved evidence.
notes: R31 targets maintenance matrix dependency. PRIMARY evidence E1 establishes an emergency override for Concrete Mixers (12-hour window) effective immediately, superseding the SRS v1.2 dynamic matrix. E4 and E5 specify the operational requirements for maintenance period management, blocking rentals, and immediate status updates. E7 and E11 identify gaps in maintenance-state representation and the missing official matrix specification. The operative context reflects the current hardcoded behavior and functional requirements; the gaps capture the pending matrix definition and UI ambiguity that must be resolved before full matrix implementation."
